assignment:
Your principal is reconsidering the school's cell phone policy. She is considering two possible policies: 
Policy 1: Allow students to bring phones to school and use them during lunch periods and other free times, as long as the phones are turned off during class time. 
Policy 2: Do not allow students to have phones at school at all.
Write a letter to your principal convincing her which policy you believe is better. Support your position with specific reasons.
essay_1:
Dear Principal,

I am writing about the cell phone policy you are thinking about changing. I think Policy 1 is the better choice. Students should be able to bring phones to school and use them at lunch and during free periods, as long as the phones stay off in class.

My first reason is safety. A lot of parents want to be able to reach their kids during the day, and kids need a way to call home when plans change. If practice gets cancelled or someone feels sick, one text takes care of it. If there is an emergency, like a lockdown or a bus accident, a phone could let a family know their kid is okay. Taking phones away completely would take that away too.

My second reason is that Policy 1 teaches responsibility. In a few years we will be in college or at jobs where nobody takes our phones. We will have to decide on our own when to put them down. Using phones at lunch and keeping them off in class gives us practice with that kind of self-control. A total ban just teaches kids to sneak.

Third, a full ban would be hard to enforce. Kids will still bring phones in their pockets and backpacks, and teachers would spend class time searching for them. With Policy 1 the rule is clear, so most students will follow it. Teachers only have to step in if a phone comes out during class.

Also, phones can be useful during free time. Students can check assignments online, look things up for a project, or text their group partners. Lunch is a time to relax, and a few minutes of music or a message from your family is a nice break in the day.

Some people say phones will distract students. Policy 1 already handles that by keeping phones off when we are learning. Students who break the rule can get a detention, and everyone else still gets to use their phones the right way.

For these reasons, I hope you pick Policy 1. It keeps us safe, it helps us grow up, and it is fair and easy to follow. I think students would really like it, and we would show you we can handle it. Thank you for listening to us.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student

Dear Principal,

I heard your thinking about changing the cell phone policy and I think Policy 1 is better. Students should get to bring phones to school and use them at lunch and free periods, as long as there off in class.

My first reason is safety. Alot of parents want to be able to reach there kids during the day and kids need a way to call home if something changes. Like if practice gets canceled or you feel sick you can just text your mom. If there was a real emergency like a lockdown or a bus crash, a phone could let your family know your ok. If you ban phones all the way parents would be way more worried.

My second reason is it teaches us to be responsible. In a few years were going to be in college or have jobs and nobody is going to take our phones away. We have to figure out on our own when to put them down. If we can use them at lunch but have to keep them off in class, thats good practice. A total ban just teaches kids to sneak them.

Third, a full ban would be really hard to enforce. Kids are still going to bring phones in there pockets and backpacks, and teachers will waste time looking for them and taking them instead of teaching. With Policy 1 the rule is clear and fair so most kids will actually follow it. Teachers only have to do something if somebody takes a phone out in class.

Also phones can help during free time. You can check your grades and assignments, look stuff up for a project, or text your group for a project. Lunch is supposed to be a time to relax to, and listening to music or texting your mom for a couple minutes doesn't hurt anybody.

Some people think phones will distract students. I get that but Policy 1 already fixes that because phones have to be off when we are learning. If someone breaks the rule they can get in trouble and everyone else still gets the good stuff.

For all these reasons I really hope you pick Policy 1. It keeps students safe, it teaches responsibility, and its easier to enforce. Thank you for reading my letter.

Sincerely,
A Concerned Student
